record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For problem (III), namely −Δu = K(x)(λu^β − u^α) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, K(x)=d(x)^{−k}, 0<k<2, and 0<α<β<1, when k−α<1 are there multiple positive solutions rather than just a single positive branch for large λ?

evidence.quote: it would be interesting to know if there is more than one positive solution in the first case k − α < 1 and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions. Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\ge 1$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $d(x) = \mathrm{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)$. Fix exponents $0 < \alpha < \beta < 1$ and a weight exponent $0 < k < 2$, and set $K(x) = d(x)^{-k}$. For $\lambda > 0$ consider the singular semilinear Dirichlet problem
$$
-\Delta u = K(x)\bigl(\lambda u^{\beta} - u^{\alpha}\bigr) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u > 0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega.
$$
Assume the parameter regime
$$
k - \alpha < 1.
$$
Question: Does there exist $\lambda^* > 0$ such that for every $\lambda > \lambda^*$ the above problem admits at least two distinct positive (weak) solutions, or is the positive solution for large $\lambda$ unique (i.e. a single positive branch)? Equivalently, characterize the multiplicity of positive solutions for large $\lambda$ in the regime $k - \alpha < 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a specific result settling multiplicity of positive solutions in the regime $k-\alpha<1$ for the equation $-\Delta u = d(x)^{-k}(\lambda u^\beta - u^\alpha)$ with $0<\alpha<\beta<1$. Related literature on singular elliptic problems with absorption and weighted singular weights addresses existence and asymptotic behavior, but no source clearly answers the specific multiplicity-for-large-$\lambda$ question, so the status appears unknown.

status_evidence.title: Multiplicity and asymptotic behavior of positive solutions for a singular semilinear elliptic problem
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiplicity for singular semilinear problems combining absorption and source terms.
status_evidence.claim: Related multiplicity results exist for analogous singular problems but not the specific weighted problem in question.

status_evidence.title: Multiplicity of singular solutions for semilinear elliptic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses multiplicity of singular solutions; does not cover the d(x)^{-k}(λu^β−u^α) absorption model in the k−α<1 regime.
status_evidence.claim: No direct resolution of the posed question is found.
